newsitem.title: USA: Chesterfield Cty, Va., approves $228 mln of GOs.
newsitem.headline: Chesterfield Cty, Va., approves $228 mln of GOs.

text.p: Chesterfield County, Va., voters approved four general obligation bond issues totaling $228.4 million, election officials said Wednesday.
On the $174.8 million bonds for schools, 76,896 voters said yes, while 16,139 said no, according to unofficial results.
For the $34 million public safety bonds, 70,861 said yes, while 19,291 voted against the measure. The proceeds will be used for a new communications system and four new fire stations.
The $10.3 million for libraries was passed by 68,801 voters, while 23,544 voted against the measure. Two new libraries will be built.
And, $9.3 million for parks was given a thumbs up by 67,266 voters and 23,799 voted against the park bond issue.
Some of the $174.8 million for the rapidly growing 56 school district neary Richmond, Va., will be used for three new schools, said Judy Davis, community relations specialist.

The 50,000 student district plans one new high school and two elementary schools as well as major renovations and additions to 10 older schools, she said. Funds will also be used for technology infrastructure and computers, she said.
It is the first bond referendum by the County since 1988.
